extracted.intended_audience: student journalists and newspaper reporters learning feature and event coverage
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for reporting and writing newspaper stories about exhibitions, shows, parades, banquets, holiday celebrations, commencements and similar special occasions, focusing on selection of detail, tone, and descriptive treatment to convey the spirit of the event.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type of story (classification)
rubrics_metrics.description: News stories in this division may be grouped in two classes: (1) those of display, such as exhibitions, shows, fairs, and parades, and (2) those of banquets, holiday celebrations, and other special occasions, such as college commencements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the subject matter covers a wide range, the method of handling the news is much the same for these classes; identify which class the event falls into to orient treatment and selection of material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose — portray events and bring out spirit
rubrics_metrics.description: The aim in these stories is not only to portray attractively the events and scenes but to bring out the spirit of the occasion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek the dominant note of the event and select details that bring out this note; accuracy here is 'truth of sentiment' as well as factual faithfulness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of details for mood (not mere recording)
rubrics_metrics.description: The selection and presentation of details from the point of view of their value as showing the mood of the occasion results in a story of much greater interest than does the mere recording of the different incidents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the large mass of available material, choose picturesque and significant phases that illustrate the mood; prefer details that support one clear impression rather than an exhaustive catalog of incidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy as truth of sentiment; avoid fictitious or sentimentalizing additions
rubrics_metrics.description: Accuracy in news stories of this kind... is not simply faithfulness to fact, but truth of sentiment. Untruthfulness lies in adding fictitious details in an effort to heighten the appeal, and in substituting sentimentality for true sentiment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not invent or embellish facts to create atmosphere; avoid sentimental language that replaces genuine observation of the event's sentiment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment — vivid, picturesque, dynamic description
rubrics_metrics.description: The chief problem in writing these stories is to select picturesque and significant phases from the large mass of available material, and to reproduce the scenes and incidents with vividness. These events offer one of the few chances in news writing for pure description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use dynamic description (details selected to bring out one impression) rather than static or exhaustive depiction; emphasize sensory, pictorial details that convey the scene.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match emotional tone to specific holiday or occasion
rubrics_metrics.description: In descriptions of holiday celebrations an emotional appeal is possible because every festival and holiday has its own particular sentiment (e.g., Christmas = children's day/generosity; Memorial Day = patriotic reverence; Fourth of July = patriotic jollification; Thanksgiving = feasting).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anchor descriptive choices and examples to the particular sentiment associated with the occasion to heighten authenticity and reader resonance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of speeches and toasts within event stories
rubrics_metrics.description: When speeches and toasts are delivered in connection with these events, they are treated like other speeches and are fitted into the story as incidents of the occasion, or, if they are of sufficient significance, they may be played up as the feature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrate notable remarks as part of the scene unless a speech itself is the newsworthy centerpiece; decide whether to summarize, quote selectively, or feature the speech based on significance.
